segments.text: IllustrisTNG is calibrated to selected local observations. This paper tests it away from that tuning point. The key move is to subtract TNG's own local residual before comparing its evolution with SDSS and JWST.

At redshift zero, TNG's star-forming main sequence sits 0.30 dex below SDSS, while its mass-metallicity relation sits 0.12 dex above. Those offsets are systematic starting errors, not high-redshift evolution.
After removing the starting error, TNG's internal main-sequence growth is plus 1.30, 1.45, and 1.61 dex at redshifts four, five, and six. Observations rise only about 0.9 to 1.0 dex.
On one electron-temperature-anchored scale, observations evolve by about minus 0.40 dex and TNG by about minus 0.27. The remaining 0.13 dex gap lies within the residual calibration systematic.

The reproducible mismatch is the over-strong growth of star formation. The chemical-evolution comparison is not significant after scale matching. Reproducing local observables neither validates the simulation nor makes every later disagreement physical.

Three datasets still require imperfect abundance-scale reconciliation, and the draft has no human clearance. This is an autonomous descriptive result, not a validated measurement. Automated review is not journal or human peer review.
